Best watches for HYROX (2026): training vs race day 
 Race day 15 min read Best fitness trackers and watches for HYROX (2026): training vs race day
 Which watches work indoors with no GPS: HYROX race modes by brand, wrist vs chest-strap heart rate, footpods, and picks for training and race day.
 By Tim Grassin , founder of RoxSkin · Last checked October 20, 2026 · 32 sources 
 The best HYROX watch is one that makes lap-taking easy indoors, paired with a chest strap if you care about heart rate. HYROX is raced inside with no usable GPS, the official splits come from the timing chip on your ankle, and wrist heart rate struggles at the sleds, carries and wall balls. So the right device for training (load, recovery, heart-rate zones) isn't always the right one for race day (big buttons, a simple screen, a reliable race mode). This guide compares the race modes that actually exist as of October 2026, explains the indoor accuracy problems, and gives picks by budget and athlete type.

 Key takeaway
 Do you even need one? No. You can finish, and race well, without a watch. Your official run, station and Roxzone splits come from the chip timing and appear in your results afterwards. A watch earns its place in training, where heart-rate zones and load help you pace and recover, and on race day only if it helps you stick to a plan without thinking.
 Why HYROX is hard for wearables
 Most sports watches are built for outdoor endurance: GPS for distance, a steady rhythm for the optical heart-rate sensor, one sport at a time. HYROX breaks all three.
 No GPS indoors, so run distance is a guess
 HYROX runs in halls and arenas, where GPS signal is weak or bounces off the roof. Turn GPS off. Without it, your watch estimates distance from your wrist movement (the accelerometer), and that estimate drifts with tight laps, turns, crowds and a tired, shorter stride. It may say you ran 7.2 km or 8.9 km. Neither number matters: the course is measured by the organisers, and you run the laps you're told to run.
 Tip
 Use lap time , not distance, to judge your runs. If you want a live indoor pace number, a footpod such as Stryd is far more consistent than the wrist, because it measures your foot directly.
 A footpod measures your foot directly, so indoor pace and distance stay consistent where wrist estimates drift. 
 Sixteen segments plus the Roxzone
 A race is 8 runs and 8 stations, with the Roxzone transition area in between. That's at least 16 segments, and more if you want transitions timed separately. Every segment change is a button press, unless your watch's race mode detects it for you. Under fatigue, people forget presses, press twice, or knock the crown with a wrist bend. One reviewer testing the Amazfit Balance 3 found forgetting to press at transitions the biggest usability problem in simulations.
 Wrist heart rate struggles at the stations
 Optical (PPG) sensors shine light into your wrist and read blood flow. They work best when the wrist is still and the rhythm is steady, like easy running. HYROX stations do the opposite:
 Sled push and pull, farmers carry: a hard grip and flexed wrist tighten the tendons under the sensor and change blood flow.
 Wall balls, burpee broad jumps, SkiErg: repeated impacts and arm swings shift the watch on your skin.
 Sweat loosens the seal between sensor and skin.
 A hard grip and a flexed wrist at the sled change blood flow under the sensor, so wrist heart rate is least reliable here. 
 The research agrees. A Cleveland Clinic study (Gillinov et al., 2017) found a chest strap matched ECG best, and optical wrist devices varied by exercise type. A 2020 study in npj Digital Medicine (Bent et al.) found optical error was around 30% higher during activity than at rest. A small 2025 study of wrist-worn Garmin watches during deadlifts found error grew at higher intensity and recommended a chest strap for resistance training. Hands-on testers report the same pattern in HYROX simulations, with wrist readings spiking or lagging in the hardest efforts.

 Knocks and buttons
 The sled handles, kettlebells and wall ball can all hit your watch. Some people wear it a little further up the forearm, or on the non-dominant wrist. Physical buttons beat touchscreens with sweaty fingers, and a button lock stops accidental pauses.
 Which brands have a HYROX or hybrid race mode? (October 2026)
 Only two big watch brands have a built-in mode designed for this format. Everyone else relies on multisport set-ups or third-party apps.
 Amazfit: the official HYROX mode
 Amazfit (Zepp Health) became HYROX's official wearable and timekeeping partner in August 2024, and in April 2026 signed a three-year global deal. It's the only brand that can call its mode "HYROX".
 What it has: a HYROX Race Mode (Single, Doubles or Relay), race simulations, a training library, Virtual Pace against a plan you build in the Zepp app, and post-race analysis with heart rate per station. Amazfit says a Stryd footpod can provide indoor run pace in Race Mode.
 Segment handling: reviewers describe pressing a button to move between runs and stations. Amazfit's own roadmap, reported by the5krunner in September 2026, schedules automatic transitions for flagship watches (including Balance 3, Active 3 Premium, T-Rex 3 and Cheetah 2 Pro) from October 2026, with Balance 2 and Active Max following in November. Roadmaps slip, so check your watch's release notes before relying on it.
 Models: Amazfit's HYROX page lists race mode on the Balance Ultra, 3 and 2, T-Rex Ultra 2, 3 Pro and 3, Cheetah 2 Pro and Ultra, Active Max, Active 3 Premium, Active 2, Bip Max and Bip 6. Older and cheaper models get fewer of the newest features.
 Helio Strap Pro: an optional upper-arm band Amazfit says adds station movement tracking and continuous arm heart rate. It needs a compatible Amazfit watch. Early reviews are cautious about how useful the extra data is.
 COROS: Hybrid Fitness mode
 COROS added a mode called Hybrid Fitness in its March 2026 update. It covers the same eight stations in the standard order, with Race, Training and Test modes.
 Segment handling: COROS says the watch can auto-detect when you move between a run and a station, or you can switch to manual transitions with the Back/Lap button. Race options include individual, doubles and relay.
 Models: PACE 4, PACE 3, PACE Pro, APEX 4, APEX 2 and 2 Pro, NOMAD, VERTIX 2 and 2S. Older models (PACE 2, APEX Pro, VERTIX 1) don't get it.
 Footpods: COROS watches pair with Stryd for indoor pace.
 Caveats: in an early test of the Test mode on an APEX 2 Pro, a reviewer pressed to change legs, still saw some per-leg times recorded wrongly, and got no rep counts. Test it in a full simulation before race day.
 Garmin: no native mode, but lots of workarounds
 As of October 2026 Garmin has no HYROX activity profile. You have three good options:
 Repeat multisport: build a two-leg profile (an indoor run with GPS off, then Cardio) and set it to repeat, with auto-lap and transitions off. Garmin's own Swedish blog describes a similar Lap-button set-up. Each segment saves separately.
 Cardio with laps: copy the Cardio profile, turn GPS off, show lap time, total time and heart rate, and press Lap at each change. Simple, one activity, no station names.
 Connect IQ apps: free and paid third-party apps (for example Hyrox Tracker, ROXZONE, RoxTrack, Hybrid Smash) add station names, 16-split recording and, in some, Roxzone timing. They're independent of HYROX and Garmin, so check compatibility and reviews.
 Garmin's real strength is training: Training Readiness, HRV Status, Training Load and Acute Load, recovery time, a strength activity with rep counting, and support for chest straps and footpods. The HRM 600 strap also stores heart rate if the connection drops.
 Apple Watch: apps do the work
 The Workout app has no HYROX workout. Options:
 Third-party apps on the App Store, such as HyRhythm, RoxWatch and others, track runs, stations and transitions, often with current and next station on screen. Quality varies, and they're independent of HYROX.
 A built-in workout with manual segments: some athletes use one workout and mark segments as they go. It's workable, but you'll get less useful data.
 Pair a Bluetooth chest strap. Apple Watch supports Bluetooth heart-rate sensors, which fixes the biggest weakness.
 Battery is the other limit: the regular Series lasts about a day, which is fine for a race but means charging habits matter in race week. The Ultra lasts considerably longer.
 Polar, Suunto and Samsung
 None has an official HYROX mode that we could find. Polar watches (Vantage V3, Grit X2) can use a custom sport profile or multisport set-up with manual laps, and Polar's H10 strap is the reference sensor in many accuracy studies. Suunto users build a custom sport mode with lap number, lap time, heart rate and total time on one screen. Samsung Galaxy Watch reviewers describe a custom multi-sport workout with manual laps. All three support external heart-rate straps.
 WHOOP and Oura: training only
 Screenless trackers can't take laps or show you anything mid-race, so they're training and recovery tools.
 WHOOP (memberships from around $149 a year) tracks strain, recovery, HRV and sleep, and its Strength Trainer feature adds muscular load from logged sets. One long-term tester found its wrist heart rate unreliable in HYROX simulations but accurate when worn on the upper arm in a sleeve. It can broadcast heart rate to a watch or gym equipment.
 Oura (Ring 4 from around $349, plus a membership of about $6 a month in the US) is strong on sleep and readiness. A ring takes a beating under kettlebell handles and sled grips, so many people take it off for heavy grip work.

 Training with a tracker: what actually matters
 Your watch is most useful in the 12 to 16 weeks before a race, not on race day.
 Heart-rate zones
 Most HYROX training is aerobic base work plus threshold intervals, and heart rate is the easiest way to keep easy days easy. Set your zones from a recent test (lactate threshold or a max-effort field test) rather than an age formula. Our VO2max calculator gives you a baseline and an 8-week plan, and how to train for HYROX explains how zones fit a weekly structure.
 Training load and readiness
 Garmin, COROS, Polar, Amazfit and WHOOP all estimate training load and recovery. They're helpful for spotting trends, like a run of red days or a load spike after you add a second sled session. Treat them as prompts, not orders. Heart-rate-based load under-counts heavy strength work, because a sled push is hard on muscles without raising heart rate for long.
 Strength tracking
 Automatic rep counting is unreliable for HYROX moves like sled pushes, lunges and burpee broad jumps. Log sets and loads yourself, or use a strength feature where you enter them (WHOOP's Strength Trainer, Garmin's strength activity). What matters is progressive overload over weeks, not the watch's rep count.
 Treadmill and indoor running
 Calibrate: Garmin lets you correct treadmill distance at the end of a run. Apple Watch improves its indoor estimate from outdoor GPS runs.
 Footpods: Stryd (around $300 for one pod; check current pricing) gives consistent indoor pace and distance on most major watches, and a reviewer found it within a few seconds per mile of the treadmill display. It's a training luxury, not a requirement.
 Lap time over pace: In compromised-running sessions (run, station, run), log lap times for each 1 km and compare them over weeks.
 Pacing by heart rate and effort
 On race day you'll pace by lap time, breathing and perceived effort (RPE), with heart rate as a check on the runs. Practise that in training: run 1 km after a sled or wall-ball set, note your time and how hard it felt, and learn what "sustainable" feels like with tired legs. Plan your target splits with the HYROX pace calculator , then read HYROX pacing and the Roxzone for how to spread the effort.
 Screenless trackers: pros and cons
 Pros
 Comfortable 24/7.
 Strong sleep and HRV data.
 Nothing to knock at the stations.
 WHOOP can sit on your upper arm.
 Cons
 No laps.
 No live data.
 No race mode.
 Monthly fees.
 A common set-up is a screenless tracker for recovery plus a simple watch or chest strap for sessions.
 Race-day set-up checklist
 Watch out
 First, the rules. The 26/27 rulebook's list of permitted items doesn't include watches, and items that aren't listed are treated as not allowed by default. The official wearable partner sells a race mode, but judges follow the rulebook, so check your event's athlete guide or ask customer service before race day. See what's not allowed at HYROX for the rest.
 If you do race with a watch:
 Build the race in advance. Use your watch's HYROX or Hybrid Fitness mode, a Connect IQ or App Store app, or a repeat multisport profile. Set it for 16 segments, or about 32 if you time each Roxzone entry and exit separately.
 Do one full or half simulation with that exact set-up at least two weeks before the race, including the button presses.
 Turn GPS and auto-lap off. They'll only give you wrong splits.
 Lock the buttons or touchscreen if your watch allows it, so a wall-ball squat doesn't pause your recording.
 Fit the strap properly. Wet the chest strap electrodes, tighten it a notch more than for running, and check it's paired before you enter the start pen.
 Charge everything the night before , including the strap if it's rechargeable.
 Keep the screen simple: total time, lap time and heart rate, in large digits. Station names are nice but not needed.
 Don't trust distance or indoor pace unless you're using a footpod.
 Afterwards, use the official results for your true splits, and your watch for heart rate by segment.
 Our race-day planner builds a race-morning timeline and checklist, and the packing list covers everything else.
 What to show on the watch face
 Main screen: lap time (biggest), total time, heart rate.
 Optional second screen: a target split for the current segment, or time of day, if your app supports a race plan.
 Leave off: distance, pace without a footpod, cadence and anything you have to scroll to.
 Common race-day mistakes
 Chasing heart rate at the stations. Wrist heart rate is least reliable there. Pace stations by effort and breathing.
 Forgetting or doubling a lap press, then spending a run trying to fix it. Leave it and keep racing.
 Pacing runs by the watch's distance. It's wrong indoors. Use lap time.
 Trying a new app or mode on race day. If you haven't simulated with it, don't race with it.
 Getting distracted by data. If checking the watch costs you focus, race by feel and review the numbers later.
 Recommendations by athlete type and budget
 First-timer, any budget: use what you have, or nothing. If you buy one thing, make it a chest strap for training. Learn pacing by effort first.
 Budget under about $150: Amazfit Active 2 for a built-in HYROX mode, or keep your current watch and add a Polar H10.
 Mid-range ($250 to $400): COROS PACE 4 or Amazfit Balance 3, both with built-in race modes and Stryd support. Add a chest strap if heart rate matters to you.
 Data-driven trainer: Garmin Forerunner 570 or 970 with an HRM 600 or H10 and a Connect IQ HYROX app. Add Stryd if you train on treadmills.
 iPhone user: keep or buy an Apple Watch (Series 12 or Ultra 4 for longer battery), add a third-party HYROX app and a Bluetooth chest strap.
 Recovery-focused or wears a ring already: WHOOP (worn on the upper arm in sessions) or Oura for sleep and readiness, plus a cheap watch or strap for workouts.
 Pro division or chasing a big PB: the watch matters less than the plan. Use it in training to keep easy work easy and threshold work honest, then race by lap time. See how to improve your HYROX time .
 FAQ
 What is the best watch for HYROX?
 There's no single best watch, because training and racing need different things. For value, the COROS PACE 4 has a built-in Hybrid Fitness race mode and good training tools. For a dedicated race mode, Amazfit (the official HYROX wearable partner) has the most complete HYROX features, such as on the Balance 3. For training and recovery data, Garmin's Forerunner range is the most thorough. Pair any of them with a chest strap for reliable heart rate.
 Does Garmin have a HYROX mode?
 Not as of October 2026. Garmin users set up a repeating multisport profile (indoor run plus Cardio), use a Cardio activity with manual laps, or install a third-party Connect IQ app that records runs, stations and sometimes Roxzone times. Check app compatibility for your model.
 Does Apple Watch have a HYROX workout?
 No, the Workout app has no HYROX workout. Third-party App Store apps track runs, stations and transitions, and you can pair a Bluetooth chest strap for better heart rate at the stations.
 Can you wear a watch during a HYROX race?
 The 26/27 rulebook's permitted list doesn't include watches, and unlisted items are prohibited by default. Check your event's athlete guide or ask customer service before race day, rather than finding out at the start line.
 Is wrist heart rate accurate during HYROX?
 It's reasonable on the runs and ergs, but often wrong at the sled push, sled pull, farmers carry and wall balls, where grip, wrist flexion and impact disturb the optical sensor. A chest strap is the most accurate option, and an upper-arm optical band is a good second choice.
 Why is my watch's run distance wrong at HYROX?
 Because there's no reliable GPS indoors, so the watch estimates distance from your arm movement. Tight laps, turns and tired running throw the estimate off. The course is measured for you, so pace by lap time, or use a footpod like Stryd for consistent indoor pace.
 Do I need a footpod for HYROX?
 No. A footpod gives more consistent pace and distance indoors and on treadmills, which helps in training. On race day, lap times and effort work fine, and your official splits come from chip timing.
 Is WHOOP or Oura good for HYROX training?
 Yes, for recovery, sleep and training load, but not for racing, because they have no screen or lap button. WHOOP's heart rate is more accurate on the upper arm than the wrist during HYROX-style sessions. Many people pair a screenless tracker with a watch or chest strap for workouts.

 Most running watches track well on a flat road. HYROX is not a flat road. You’re transitioning between 8 km of running and 8 functional stations inside an exhibition hall — and the best watch for HYROX needs to keep up with all of it. Here’s what separates a genuinely useful HYROX watch from one that becomes dead weight on your wrist.
 GPS and Indoor Tracking 
 HYROX races happen indoors, which is the enemy of GPS accuracy. The 1 km running loops run inside convention centers and exhibition halls with heavy metal infrastructure. A watch that relies solely on satellite signal will show wildly inaccurate distances — making any pace data essentially useless.
 The best watch for HYROX offers an accelerometer-based indoor running mode or foot pod compatibility (such as Stryd). Amazfit’s dedicated HYROX mode handles indoor tracking natively — a real advantage over most competitors on this list.
 Heart Rate Accuracy Under Load 
 During sled pushes and burpee broad jumps, your wrist position shifts constantly. Optical wrist HR sensors struggle under these conditions. The best watch for HYROX either has an exceptionally stable HR sensor or supports Bluetooth chest strap pairing for accurate zone data across every station.
 💡 
 Info 
 Pairing any watch with a chest strap (like the Garmin HRM-Pro or Polar H10) dramatically improves heart rate accuracy during functional stations. If you’re serious about pacing by zone, this $60–$80 accessory matters more than upgrading your watch model.
 Durability and Button Control 
 Touchscreens and sweat don’t mix. During a 1,000m row or a set of wall balls, you need to lap your watch with a single button press — without looking down for more than half a second. Every option in our best watch for HYROX list has physical buttons for exactly this reason.
 Durability matters too. Sled push grip pressure and sandbag lunges put real stress on watch bezels. Gorilla Glass or sapphire crystal lenses are worth the premium if you race more than once a year. If your legs take the same beating during those stations, a compression leg sleeve for HYROX is worth the same consideration as your watch bezel.
 Battery Life 
 A HYROX race lasts between 60 and 180 minutes depending on your level. Race-day battery survival is never the real question. What matters is whether your watch handles 3–4 weeks of daily training without stress. Every best watch for HYROX pick on this list survives race day comfortably — battery life differentiates training comfort, not race survival.
 The 7 Best Watches for HYROX in 2026 
 Every watch below was selected on four criteria: indoor tracking quality, HR accuracy under functional load, physical usability during stations, and value for money at its price point. These are the best watch for HYROX options available right now.
 1. Amazfit Cheetah Pro — Best Overall Watch for HYROX 
 Price range: ~$220–$250 
 If you want the single best watch for HYROX without spending Fenix money, this is it. Amazfit is the official global wearable partner of HYROX — and the Cheetah Pro is the only watch with a dedicated built-in HYROX Race Mode that tracks all 8 stations, the running segments, and transitions in one structured workout. No manual mode switching between the SkiErg and the run — the watch manages it automatically.
 The Cheetah Pro uses dual-band GPS with BioTracker 4.0 optical HR. For indoor running accuracy, it supports Stryd foot pod integration — solving the GPS drift problem every other watch faces inside a convention center. The AMOLED display stays readable under sweat, and the physical crown button gives you reliable lap control mid-station. As the best watch for HYROX at its price point, the Cheetah Pro offers functionality no competitor matches below $400.
 ✅ 
 Best For 
 Athletes who want a purpose-built HYROX experience without paying premium prices. The dedicated race mode alone saves significant setup time and gives you cleaner post-race splits than any manually configured multisport profile.
 2. Garmin Forerunner 265 — Best Watch for HYROX Running-Focused Athletes 
 Price range: ~$350–$400 
 For athletes whose HYROX race lives or dies by running pace — and for most people it does — the Forerunner 265 is the best watch for HYROX in the mid-range Garmin lineup. At approximately 47g, it’s the lightest watch on this list, which means zero arm swing interference during running segments. The AMOLED screen performs excellently in low-light indoor venues.
 Garmin added a HYROX Activity Profile via firmware update, letting you track race segments with more structure than a generic multisport mode. Training load analysis, VO2 Max tracking, and race predictor tools make this the strongest daily training companion on the list. It’s not as plug-and-play as the Amazfit for race day, but for the 12 weeks of training before the gun goes off, nothing matches it at this price.
 Pair the data this watch generates with a structured training block. Our complete HYROX training guide shows exactly how to use pace and HR data to structure your build-up.
 3. Garmin Fenix 8 (47mm) — Best Premium Watch for HYROX 
 Price range: ~$700–$900 
 The Fenix 8 is overkill for most HYROX athletes — but if you also run ultras or triathlons, it’s the most complete tool on the market. As the best watch for HYROX at the premium end, the sapphire crystal lens, titanium casing, and MIL-STD-810 durability rating mean it handles every station with zero damage risk. Dual-frequency multi-band GPS delivers the best indoor/outdoor tracking available in any consumer watch.
 In practice, the Fenix 8 gives you ecosystem depth and longevity rather than HYROX-specific features the Forerunner 265 can’t already match. Only consider it if you’re a confirmed multi-sport athlete who wants one watch for the next decade.
 4. Coros Pace 3 — Best Budget Watch for HYROX 
 Price range: ~$200–$230 
 At under $230, the Coros Pace 3 is the best budget watch for HYROX on the market. Dual-frequency GPS, a multisport mode, and one of the best battery lives in its class — up to 17 days smartwatch mode, 38 hours GPS mode — make it a standout value for athletes entering their first race without wanting to overspend on gear.
 The dial-style physical button is one of the most reliable lap controls available — no accidental screen presses during the farmers carry or wall balls. What it lacks is a native HYROX mode and the analytical depth of Garmin’s platform. You’ll need to configure a custom multisport profile manually once, which takes about 10 minutes and works seamlessly on race day. For pure cost-per-feature value, nothing beats it as a best watch for HYROX entry point.

 Warning 
 The Coros Pace 3 comes with a nylon band as standard. It’s comfortable for training but absorbs sweat heavily during a full HYROX race. Pick up a spare silicone strap before race day — widely available for under $15.
 5. Apple Watch Ultra 3 — Best Watch for HYROX Apple Ecosystem Users 
 Price range: ~$800–$900 
 If your entire life runs through an iPhone, the Apple Watch Ultra 3 is a capable best watch for HYROX option — though not for purely sport-specific reasons. The Action Button delivers one-press lap control with wet hands, the titanium case is the most impact-resistant on this list, and up to 36 hours battery in low-power mode is a real step forward over older Apple Watch generations.
 The core limitation is indoor GPS. Apple Watch relies heavily on satellite signal, which degrades significantly inside large metal exhibition halls. Third-party apps like ROXFIT or Runna improve the training experience considerably. If you’re buying a best watch for HYROX from scratch with no existing ecosystem, a Garmin or Amazfit will serve you better at the same or lower price.

 Price range: ~$280–$320 
 HYROX training is high-volume and high-intensity. The biggest mistake most intermediate athletes make isn’t under-training — it’s failing to recover properly between sessions. Its main limitations are average indoor tracking and no native HYROX mode. But for athletes who overtrain or struggle with recovery windows between race-pace sessions, this is the smartest best watch for HYROX choice on this list.

It lacks the advanced training load metrics of the 265, and the HR sensor is slightly less accurate under high-intensity station work — but as the best entry-level watch for HYROX, it covers every essential: GPS, lap tracking, heart rate zones, and a battery that lasts well beyond your training week.
 If you’re on your first HYROX race prep and haven’t committed to a premium watch yet, the 165 is the cleanest entry point in the Garmin lineup. Use it to understand which features you actually need in training — that knowledge will drive a smarter upgrade decision later.

Both cost under $230, both track everything you need for your first race, and neither will overwhelm you with data you can’t yet interpret. Focus on finishing your first event, then decide on an upgrade. Read our guide on what no one tells you before your first HYROX race to understand what else to prepare.
 If You’re Intermediate and Racing Seriously 
 The best watch for HYROX at the intermediate level is the Amazfit Cheetah Pro — it delivers purpose-built HYROX tracking at a price no Garmin can match. If running analysis matters more than a native race mode, the Garmin Forerunner 265 is worth the extra $150 and remains the best watch for HYROX in the Garmin mid-range lineup.
 If Budget Is the Priority 
 The best watch for HYROX on a tight budget is the Coros Pace 3 — no contest. Set up a custom multisport profile once before race day and you have everything you need for under $230. Don’t let gear purchasing delay your actual training. More time running and doing station work will improve your finish time far more than any watch feature.
 If you train across several disciplines beyond HYROX, HybridPace has a roundup of the best fitness trackers for hybrid athletes .
 🚨 
 Important 
 No best watch for HYROX fixes a bad pacing strategy. Going out too fast on runs 1–3 and blowing up from station 5 onward is the most common race-day mistake. Your watch only helps if your strategy is right behind it. See our HYROX running pace guide before race day.
 Common Mistakes When Choosing the Best Watch for HYROX 
 Most athletes overthink the best watch for HYROX decision — or make it for the wrong reasons. Here are the five most common errors to avoid.
 Buying based on brand alone. Garmin is excellent, but an Amazfit with a native HYROX mode gives you better race-day data than a Garmin without one properly configured.
 Ignoring indoor GPS limitations. Most standard GPS watches drift indoors. If your race is inside a metal exhibition hall, a foot pod or dedicated indoor mode isn’t optional — it’s essential for clean splits.
 Prioritizing touchscreen over buttons. Touchscreens are fine for navigating menus. During wall balls or a sled push, they’re a liability. The best watch for HYROX always has physical lap and start/stop buttons.
 Forgetting to charge before race day. This sounds obvious. It happens more than you’d think. Build a pre-race checklist that includes watch charge status. Our full HYROX gear guide covers complete race day prep.
 Spending premium budget on a watch instead of race experience. A $900 watch won’t improve your station times. Train more. Race more. Upgrade when you know exactly what data you’re missing.
 Quick Action Plan: Set Up Your Best Watch for HYROX 
 Once you’ve chosen the best watch for HYROX that fits your budget and profile, here’s how to configure it properly before race day — whether you have a dedicated HYROX mode or need to build a custom multisport profile from scratch.
 Activate or create your HYROX profile. If your watch has a native HYROX mode (Amazfit), activate it directly. If not, build a custom multisport profile: Run → Transition → Functional Workout, repeating 8 times.
 Set auto-lap to 1 km. This gives you automatic splits on every running segment and tells you exactly where you stand against your target pace after each loop.
 Configure heart rate zone alerts. Set a high HR ceiling alert — typically top of Zone 4 — so your watch warns you before you redline on the early running segments.
 Test your setup indoors before race day. Run a full station simulation in your gym with your watch active. Verify that lap control works with wet hands and that HR readings stay stable during sled-style movements.
 Pair a chest strap if HR precision matters. A Bluetooth HR chest strap paired with the best watch for HYROX you choose is a $60–$80 upgrade that outperforms any optical wrist sensor during functional work.
 Charge to 100% the night before. Set a phone reminder. No exceptions, no “it’s probably fine.”
 Simplify your data fields for race day. Display only: current HR, lap time, current pace, total elapsed time. Less scrolling, more racing.

 For official race formats, station requirements, and division rules, refer to the official HYROX website .

 Do I need a special watch for HYROX? 
 You don’t need a specialist watch to compete in HYROX — any GPS watch with heart rate tracking will let you race. However, the best watch for HYROX will have physical buttons, reliable indoor tracking, and a multisport or dedicated race mode that gives you significantly more useful data. The Amazfit Cheetah Pro is currently the only option with a fully native HYROX race mode built in.
 Is the Amazfit really the best watch for HYROX? 
 Amazfit is the official global wearable partner of HYROX, and the Cheetah Pro’s dedicated race mode gives it a clear race-day advantage. For pure running analysis and long-term training load management, Garmin’s ecosystem remains deeper. The best watch for HYROX ultimately depends on whether you prioritize race-day simplicity (Amazfit) or training data depth (Garmin Forerunner 265).
 Can I use an Apple Watch for HYROX? 
 Yes. The Apple Watch Ultra 3 is capable for HYROX, especially for athletes already in the Apple ecosystem. Its main limitations are indoor GPS accuracy and the absence of a native HYROX mode. Third-party apps like ROXFIT help significantly. But if you’re choosing the best watch for HYROX from scratch, a Garmin or Amazfit will serve you better at the same or lower price point.
 What is the best Garmin watch for HYROX? 
 The Garmin Forerunner 265 is the best Garmin watch for HYROX at the mid-range price point. It’s lightweight, features an AMOLED display, supports a HYROX activity profile via firmware update, and provides excellent training load analytics. If budget is open and you’re a multi-sport athlete, the Fenix 8 is the most complete Garmin available — though heavier and significantly more expensive.
 Does a watch actually improve HYROX performance? 
 Indirectly, yes. The best watch for HYROX gives you real-time pacing data that prevents going out too fast — the single most common mistake in the race. Heart rate zone alerts stop you from redlining before station 4. Post-race splits help you identify where you’re losing the most time. None of that makes you fitter, but it makes you smarter. See our guide on where most athletes lose time in HYROX to understand which stations to target.
 What is the best budget watch for HYROX? 
 The Coros Pace 3 at ~$210 is the best budget watch for HYROX. Dual-frequency GPS, a reliable physical dial button, multisport mode, and exceptional battery life make it exceptional value. You’ll need to manually configure a custom HYROX multisport profile — about 10 minutes of setup — and it works cleanly on race day. For new athletes, it covers every essential without overspending on features you won’t use for months.

 Pair the watch with your target splits from our free pace band generator and you can check each lap against plan.

 HYROX features: a race mode for the 8 stations and 1 km runs, a PFT benchmark, a HYROX training library, virtual pacing, and singles, doubles and relay formats.

 Cardio profile, GPS off: press lap at each station exit. The simplest option.

 Garmin updates its watches often, so check for newer HYROX support before you build a profile.

 Sundried names the Coros Pace 3 as a lightweight, budget-friendly alternative to the Garmin Fenix. the5krunner notes Coros has only limited HYROX multisport support , so expect the simple lap-button approach.

 You already train on Garmin or want the most apps: stay with Garmin and set up a lap profile.

 Display: current pace + heart rate + elapsed time — the three metrics that matter
 GPS mode: high accuracy — don’t use power-saving GPS for a race
 Notifications off — silence your phone connection during the race
 Fully charged — charge to 100% the night before
 Do You Need a GPS Watch for HYROX?
 No — you can pace by feel and complete a HYROX race without one. But for most athletes, a GPS watch significantly improves pacing discipline, particularly in the first half of the race when the atmosphere makes you want to run faster than you should. At a $200 entry point (Forerunner 55), the cost-to-benefit is excellent for any serious HYROX athlete.
 FAQ
 Can I wear my watch during the sled push and carries?
 Yes — all the watches listed are rated for the impact and load of HYROX training and racing. Garmin watches in particular are built to military durability standards.
 Does a chest strap HR monitor give better results?
 Slightly — chest straps are more accurate during high-intensity exercise than wrist-based optical HR. But the difference is modest, and for HYROX pacing purposes wrist-based HR on a modern Garmin is accurate enough. Only worth adding a chest strap if you’re training very precisely to HR zones.
 Which watch does the HYROX app connect to?
 The HYROX app uses manual data entry and doesn’t directly sync with GPS watches. Your watch records your data independently — review your Garmin Connect or Apple Health data after the race for splits and HR analysis.

 What does HYROX support mean on the Bip 6? 
 On the Bip 6, HYROX support is verified primarily as a selectable HYROX Race workout mode. Amazfit also lists relevant activities such as running, rowing, stair climbing, spinning, indoor fitness, cross-training, strength training, and HIIT in the watch’s broader activity catalog.

 How useful is the Bip 6 for HYROX running? 
 The Bip 6 is potentially useful for outdoor easy runs, tempo sessions, longer aerobic runs, and repeated running intervals because the watch has onboard GPS and running-related workout modes. A user can review distance, elapsed time, heart rate, and other workout information after a session through the watch and Zepp app.
 GPS performance is not guaranteed to be equally good in every HYROX-related setting. Treadmills and indoor tracks will not provide the same GPS data as an outdoor route. GPS can also be less dependable inside exhibition halls, arenas, gyms, and other partially enclosed venues. Tall buildings, crowded event areas, and a delayed satellite lock can further affect recorded distance and pace.
 For outdoor preparation, the Bip 6 should cover the basics. For race day, an athlete should not assume that the watch’s outdoor GPS distance will remain precise inside an enclosed venue. A useful pre-race test is to run the intended indoor or outdoor workout with the same display, heart-rate, and notification settings that will be used at the event.
 Can the Bip 6 track HYROX strength and functional training? 
 The Bip 6 can support strength preparation by tracking repetitions, sets, and rest periods, while the Zepp app can be used to plan workouts and synchronize those workouts to the watch. Amazfit advertises automatic detection for 25 exercise types, which is meaningful at this price but narrower than the complete range of movements an athlete may use in HYROX preparation.
 The feature set is relevant to rowing, lunges, carries, wall-ball practice, general strength work, and conditioning circuits. However, the existence of a strength mode or automatic exercise detection does not prove that the watch will correctly identify every wall ball, sled push, sled pull, farmer’s carry, or transition. Grip changes, wrist flexion, rapid movement, and equipment contact can all make wrist-based movement detection difficult.
 When automatic recognition fails, manual selection of the closest activity mode is the safer approach. Athletes should treat the resulting data as a training log and feedback aid rather than as an official station record.
 How reliable are the Bip 6 heart-rate and recovery features?

The watch and Zepp app can provide workout and recovery-related statistics, making the Bip 6 useful for observing broad trends such as whether sleep or recovery habits are worsening during a hard training block.
 Wrist optical heart-rate readings can be less reliable during gripping, pushing, pulling, rapid arm movement, sweat, vibration, or a poorly fitted band. Those conditions occur frequently in HYROX training. A watch may record a delayed, interrupted, or unusually low heart rate during sled work, rowing, carries, or other exercises that strongly flex the wrist.
 The official product listing indicates support for certain peripheral devices, including heart-rate belts and running or cycling power meters. Athletes who need more dependable heart-rate data during high-intensity intervals should consider a compatible external heart-rate belt rather than assuming that the wrist sensor will be equally reliable for every station.

 How good is the Bip 6 battery for race preparation? 
 Amazfit advertises up to 14 days of typical use, up to 26 days in power-saver mode, and approximately 1.5 to 2.5 hours for a full charge. The official Bip 6 specifications support those figures.
 Long claimed battery life is one of the Bip 6’s clearest practical advantages. A competitor can use the watch for daily workouts, sleep tracking, notifications, and general activity monitoring without charging every night. Reduced charging frequency also lowers the chance of arriving at a training session with a dead watch.
 The 14-day figure is a typical-use estimate, not a promise of 14 days of continuous GPS training. GPS activity, continuous heart-rate monitoring, frequent screen activation, phone calls, high brightness, notifications, and repeated workouts can reduce actual endurance. Before a race, charge the watch fully and disable unnecessary calls or notifications if maximum battery life matters.
 Is the Bip 6 comfortable and durable enough for HYROX? 
 The Bip 6 has a 1.97-inch AMOLED display, 5 ATM water resistance, and a lightweight construction. TechRadar lists the watch at 27.9 grams without the strap and describes it as comfortable during exercise.
 The AMOLED display should make workout information easier to see than a small, low-contrast panel, but outdoor readability still depends on brightness, reflections, and the amount of movement. Readability during a transition should be tested during actual circuits rather than assumed from the screen size alone.
 A secure strap matters during burpees, carries, rowing, sled work, and repeated wrist movement. The 5 ATM rating is useful protection against sweat, rain, and swimming-related exposure, but 5 ATM water resistance is not a guarantee against every high-impact or high-pressure situation. Training durability and comfort are not the same as formal certification that a watch is approved or required for every official event environment.
 What does “140-plus workouts” actually tell you? 
 The Bip 6’s more than 140 workout modes demonstrate breadth, not depth. A large activity catalog gives users many labels under which to record exercise, but it does not mean that every mode has a unique sensor profile, specialized metrics, or sport-specific coaching.
 For a HYROX athlete, the important modes are the ones connected to actual preparation: HYROX Race, outdoor and indoor running, rowing, strength training, HIIT, cross-training, stair climbing, and indoor fitness. Those modes are more useful than the headline number itself because they map to the demands of hybrid training.
 The buyer should ask what each selected mode records, whether the information is visible during the workout, and how the Zepp app presents it afterward. Best Garmin Watch for HYROX (2026): What Actually Matters 
 Short answer
 The best Garmin watch for HYROX runs Connect IQ apps and has a LAP button you can press by feel. As of October 2026, no Garmin has a HYROX mode, so the app matters more than the model. For most athletes, that's a five-button Forerunner: the Forerunner 70 or 170 for value, or the Forerunner 970 for a bigger screen.
 Key takeaways 
 Our picks as of October 2026: the Forerunner 70 or 170 for value, the 47 mm Forerunner 570 or the 970 for a bigger screen, the 51 mm fēnix 9 for battery and the Instinct 3 AMOLED for buttons only.
 On five-button Garmins such as the Forerunner 70, 570 and 970, the lower-right button records a lap, so you can press it by feel.
 The vívoactive 6 and Venu 4 have two buttons and a touchscreen, while the Instinct 3 AMOLED has five buttons and no touchscreen at all.
 Battery barely matters for HYROX: the lowest GPS rating among the Garmins compared here is 15 hours, on the 41 mm Venu 4.
 What is the best Garmin watch for HYROX?
 For most HYROX athletes, the best Garmin watch is a five-button Forerunner that runs Connect IQ apps. Connect IQ is Garmin's platform and store for third-party watch apps, data fields and watch faces.
 A pricier model doesn't track the race better on its own. Already own a Garmin? Look up your model in our HYROX compatibility table before you buy anything.
 We compared Garmin's current watches on the criteria below, using their owner's manuals (August and September 2026) and dated launch prices. We didn't test them on a device. Our picks:
 Best value: Forerunner 70 or 170
 The Forerunner 70 and 170 are the best Garmins for HYROX on a budget. Both have five buttons, with LAP on the lower right, and a touchscreen you can switch off for each activity.
 The Forerunner 70 launched in May 2026 at £219.99 / US$249.99, with up to 23 hours of GPS. The Forerunner 170 launched the same month at £259.99 / US$299.99, with up to 20 hours.
 Bigger screen: Forerunner 570 or 970
 The 47 mm Forerunner 570 and the Forerunner 970 have 1.4-inch screens, and both manuals list Mixed Session. Mixed Session is a generic Garmin multisport activity on newer watches that saves several activities as one.
 They launched in May 2025 at £459.99 / US$549.99 and £629.99 / US$749.99.
 Premium: fēnix 9
 The fēnix 9 comes in 43, 47 and 51 mm. Its August 2026 manual rates the 51 mm at up to 54 hours in an activity and lists Mixed Session. It launched in August 2026 from £859.99 / US$999.99.
 No touchscreen: Instinct 3 AMOLED
 The Instinct 3 AMOLED has five buttons and no touchscreen, so nothing on the screen can be tapped by mistake. Its manual rates it at up to 32 hours of GPS in 45 mm and 40 hours in 50 mm. It launched in January 2025 from £389.99 / US$449.99.
 If you prefer a touchscreen: vívoactive 6 or Venu 4
 The vívoactive 6 and Venu 4 have two buttons and a touchscreen, so fewer buttons than a Forerunner. The vívoactive 6 launched in April 2025 at £279.99 / US$299.99. The Venu 4 launched in September 2025 at £469.99 / US$549.99 and adds Mixed Session.
 For smaller wrists, the Forerunner 570 comes in 42 mm, the fēnix 9 in 43 mm and the Venu 4 in 41 mm.
 Garmin watches for HYROX compared: price, buttons, battery
 Which Garmin is best for HYROX depends less on the model than on these criteria:
 a LAP button you can press by feel
 touch you can switch off or lock
 Connect IQ support, so a HYROX app can run the race format
 battery for your longest sessions
 chest-strap pairing, for heart rate at the stations
 a screen you can read mid-station

GPS battery is each manual's GPS-only figure, except the fēnix 9. ¹ The fēnix 9 manual gives no GPS-only figure; this is its "Activity mode (Normal or Balanced power mode)" rating. 
 Every watch in the table runs Hybrid Smash. The five-button models are the safest choice, and the Forerunner 70 already has everything the race needs from the watch itself.
 Every watch in the table also lists Obstacle Racing, a Garmin running activity where you press LAP to mark the start and end of each obstacle. The Instinct manual marks obstacles with SET instead, and says some activities are Tactical Edition only.
 Will your Garmin run a HYROX app?
 Most current Garmin watches can run a HYROX app from the Connect IQ store. Hybrid Smash runs on most current Forerunner, fēnix, epix, Enduro, Venu and vívoactive models, plus the Instinct 3 AMOLED. Check your model on the Connect IQ listing or in the compatibility table .
 We make Hybrid Smash, so its device support on this page comes straight from that live listing, checked 7 October 2026.
 The Roxzone is the transition area between the running course and the workout stations. For HYROX race day on a Garmin, Hybrid Smash's Race Day mode times every run, station and Roxzone with one LAP press per changeover, using the race format and the station targets for your weight class, and saves the race to Garmin Connect.
 Hybrid Smash has the features a HYROX athlete actually uses, from Roxzone splits and pacing to undo and Garmin Connect sync, without menus to get lost in.
 Two settings on race day. You choose your target pace and Run Type ; everything else follows the race format and your weight class.
 No account. You buy it once in Garmin's Connect IQ store, with the Garmin account you already have: €9.99 / US$8.49 as of October 2026, and prices vary by region.
 Other HYROX apps add extras that Hybrid Smash leaves out on purpose. One is ROXZONE's goal-time Race Plan, built on its website, according to its Connect IQ listing (checked October 2026). RoxTrack is listed as free (October 2026). Compare the HYROX apps for Garmin .
 Is an older Forerunner or fēnix still good for HYROX?
 Yes, if it runs a Connect IQ HYROX app. As of October 2026, Hybrid Smash runs on the Forerunner 165, 255, 265, 955 and 965 and the vívoactive 5. It also runs on the fēnix 7 and 8, the epix (Gen 2) and the epix Pro.
 What older models lack is Garmin's own fallback. The Forerunner 165, 255, 265, 955 and 965 and vívoactive 5 manuals list neither Mixed Session nor Obstacle Racing. The fēnix 7 manual lists Obstacle Racing only, and the fēnix 8 manual lists both.
 Hybrid Smash isn't available for the Forerunner 55, 245, 745 or 945. On those, record a run with GPS off and Auto Pause off, and press LAP at every changeover. HYROX on every Forerunner, model by model covers each one.
 Why does a physical LAP button matter in HYROX?
 In HYROX you press the LAP button at every changeover, mid-effort and often without looking. On every five-button watch compared here, the lower-right button records a lap during an activity, according to their manuals. It sits in the same place on each, so you can find it by feel.
 On a five-button Garmin, LAP is the lower-right button, and the warm-up screen points straight at it. 
 Hybrid Smash doesn't detect stations automatically: you press LAP at every changeover. The app already knows what comes next, so each press closes one segment and names the next.
 With Race Day, a full race is 32 LAP presses with Rox Zones (the setting that times each Roxzone) on, or 17 with it off.
 Hybrid Smash uses three controls: LAP for the next segment, DOWN to undo a mistaken press and SELECT for the menu ( the in-workout menu in the user guide ). A short buzz confirms every LAP press, so you don't have to look at the watch.
 That undo matters. The Forerunner 970 manual says Garmin's own lap undo isn't available in gym activities or workouts.
 Is a touchscreen Garmin a problem in HYROX?
 A touchscreen Garmin is fine for HYROX if you can switch touch off or lock it. Each watch compared here gives you a way:
 Forerunner 70, 170, 570 and 970: their manuals let you set the touchscreen for each activity profile. The fēnix 9 lets you turn it off too.
 Instinct 3 AMOLED: there's no touchscreen, so the five buttons do everything.
 vívoactive 6 and Venu 4: two buttons plus the touchscreen. Both manuals, including the Venu 4 manual , offer Touch Lock "to prevent inadvertent screen touches".
 On a touchscreen watch, Hybrid Smash's Touch Gestures setting turns touch on or off on the workout screen, and the menus always accept touch. With Touch Gestures on, a swipe down does the same as LAP, and a swipe up undoes.
 Touch Gestures sits in Hybrid Smash's Settings, between Prioritize Pace and Rox Zones. 
 On a vívoactive or Venu, the buttons work differently from a five-button watch, so check your manual first. Here's how to set up a vívoactive or Venu for HYROX .
 Do you need Mixed Session for HYROX?
 No. You don't need Mixed Session for HYROX if you use a Connect IQ app. Each Mixed Session switch takes a stop, a Next Activity pick and a restart.
 Mixed Session gives you no station names, no station targets and no Roxzone split. A Connect IQ app runs the race sequence instead, on watches with or without Mixed Session. So treat Mixed Session as a backup, not a reason to pay more.
 How much battery does a HYROX race need?
 Every current Garmin compared here outlasts a HYROX race: the lowest GPS rating is up to 15 hours, on the 41 mm Venu 4.
 Indoors, GPS stays off. Hybrid Smash's Indoor and Cardio Run Types use no GPS, while Outdoor turns it on and uses more battery.
 Always On Display cuts battery life. The 45 mm Instinct 3 AMOLED is rated for up to 18 days as a smartwatch with Wrist Gesture, but up to 7 days with Always On Display.
 If you want battery for longer sports too, the 51 mm fēnix 9 goes furthest of the Garmins compared here. Compare the fēnix, epix and Enduro models for HYROX .
 Do you need a chest strap for HYROX?
 You don't need a chest strap to time a HYROX race, but a strap is likely to give steadier heart rate at the stations. SkiErg, Sled Pull, Rowing, Farmers Carry and Wall Balls all load your grip and wrist, where wrist readings are likely least reliable.
 Every watch compared here pairs a chest strap. Their manuals say that if wrist and chest heart rate are both available when you start an activity, the watch uses the chest data.
 In Garmin's own running activities, the HRM 600, HRM-Fit and HRM-Pro can also supply indoor pace on compatible watches, but they calibrate on outdoor runs only.
 Hybrid Smash uses your watch's heart-rate source, including a paired chest strap. The watch summary shows times. Heart rate per segment (average and max) is in the shared web breakdown.
 Which Garmin screen is easiest to read mid-race?
 The easiest Garmin screen to read mid-race is a larger AMOLED screen that's awake when you glance at it. Every watch compared here has an AMOLED screen. The largest are 1.4 inches across: the Forerunner 970, the 47 mm Forerunner 570, the 45 mm Venu 4 and the 47 and 51 mm fēnix 9.
 Garmin's AMOLED watches turn the screen off after a timeout to limit burn-in. You wake it by turning your wrist or pressing a button, or by tapping the screen on touchscreen models. You can set the display separately for activities, so check that setting before race day.
 What the screen shows matters as much as its size. Hybrid Smash keeps the watch screen to what you need right now: what you're on, how long you've been on it, and what comes next.
 The pace band turns blue when you're on target, and the line below shows what comes next. 
 Should you buy an Amazfit instead of a Garmin for HYROX?
 Buy an Amazfit instead of a Garmin only if you want a HYROX race mode built into the watch. If you already own a Garmin, a Connect IQ app such as Hybrid Smash adds the race format instead. You press LAP once per changeover, and Garmin Connect stores the station name with each lap.
 Amazfit became HYROX's exclusive wearables partner in a three-year global deal announced on 15 April 2026. As of October 2026, several Amazfit watches have a HYROX race mode. In its Amazfit Balance 3 review , the5krunner says the race mode "automatically advances as it detects changes in motion patterns", but didn't test race mode itself.
 COROS has a Hybrid Fitness mode, but it isn't HYROX-branded (the5krunner, 31 March 2026). Amazfit vs Garmin for HYROX weighs switching against keeping your Garmin.
 Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX: what can each track?
 As of October 2026, neither Garmin nor Apple Watch has a HYROX workout type built in. Both can time a race split by split.
 A Garmin times splits with its LAP button or a Connect IQ app. An Apple Watch uses workout segments or an App Store app.
 Garmin (Forerunner 70, 570, 970) Apple Watch 
 HYROX workout type None None in Apple's list of workout types 
 Mark a split Press the lower-right button Tap Segment or double-tap the display; Ultra models can use the Action button in running workouts 
 Change activity mid-session Mixed Session on the 570 and 970: stop, Next Activity, pick, start Tap New and pick another workout type

 Hybrid Smash isn't available for Apple Watch: it runs only on Garmin watches, through Connect IQ. On Apple Watch, RoxLane is one App Store option. Its listing describes a 16-segment race timer with Roxzone tracking (checked 7 October 2026).
 For marking splits, Apple Watch relies on the screen, apart from the Ultra's Action button in running workouts. A five-button Garmin uses a physical button. If you already own either, both can time a HYROX race.
 Hybrid Smash Garmin Connect IQ app 
 What is Hybrid Smash?
 Hybrid Smash is a Garmin Connect IQ watch app that tracks and paces HYROX races, simulations and workouts while you do them. One press of the LAP button per changeover, and every run, station and Roxzone is timed, labelled and saved to Garmin Connect.
 It is a one-time purchase on the Connect IQ store with no account, no subscription and no phone needed while you train. It offers Race Day (the official sequence of 8 × 1 km runs and 8 stations, with station targets for your weight class), Hyrox Sim, Free Training (pick the next station on the watch as you go), 8 ready-made HYROX workouts and 3 custom workouts.
 It is built for the balance between simplicity and the right features: a clean screen, few options and a design nobody needs a tutorial for.
 Three controls run the session: LAP for the next segment, DOWN to undo a mistaken press, SELECT for the menu.
 Saved to Garmin Connect as Indoor Run, Outdoor Run or Cardio, depending on the Run Type you pick, with every segment as a lap.
 Works on most current Garmin watches , including Forerunner, fēnix, epix, Venu and vívoactive models. Check your model on the Connect IQ store .
 Get Hybrid Smash on the Connect IQ store Read the user guide 
 FAQ
 Is there a HYROX Garmin watch?
 No. As of October 2026, no Garmin watch has a HYROX mode or activity profile, and HYROX's exclusive wearables partner is Amazfit. To track HYROX on a Garmin, press LAP at every changeover in a built-in activity, or install a Connect IQ app such as Hybrid Smash. Hybrid Smash doesn't detect stations automatically: you still press LAP at every changeover, and it names every run, station and Roxzone.
 Did the Forerunner 265 get a HYROX profile?
 No. At least one buyer guide, checked on 6 October 2026, says a firmware update added a "HYROX Activity Profile" to the Forerunner 265. The Forerunner 265 manual (June 2025) never mentions HYROX, and as of October 2026 no Garmin watch has a HYROX profile. The Forerunner 265 can still run Connect IQ HYROX apps such as Hybrid Smash: the Forerunner 265 section of our Forerunner guide covers its real options.
 Do you need a special watch for HYROX?
 No. Any Garmin that records laps can time a HYROX race if you press LAP at every changeover. A Connect IQ app such as Hybrid Smash adds the race format and names every run, station and Roxzone. The HYROX 26/27 Singles rulebook (version of 14 September 2026) bans phones on the race floor, so whatever tracks your race has to run on the watch itself.
 Does GPS matter for HYROX?
 No, not at an indoor venue: Garmin's manuals say "GPS is turned off for indoor activities". Hybrid Smash's Race Day starts on the Indoor Run Type, which uses no GPS. On Indoor, pace and distance come from your watch's wrist sensor, which is an estimate: pace reads --:-- until you're moving. A paired footpod gives more reliable indoor pace. For an outdoor course, the Outdoor Run Type uses GPS.

 Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX: What Matters on Race Day 
 A running watch is built for one sport. HYROX asks it to follow eight 1 km runs, eight stations and the Roxzone between them, indoors, with sweaty and sometimes chalky hands. Official times come from the chip on your ankle, so your watch is there for pacing, heart rate and your own post-race analysis.
 A HYROX-ready watch needs six things: 
 A lap or segment button that works with wet, chalky hands
 An indoor mode with GPS off, so distance drift cannot ruin your splits
 A way to separate runs, stations and Roxzone time (built-in mode, multisport profile or app)
 Stable heart rate, or support for a chest strap
 Battery that lasts well beyond a race and a hard training week
 A screen you can read at a glance under arena lights
 Everything below scores the Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX contest against that list. Each section is one check, so you can jump to the one that matters most to you.
 Check 1: HYROX Setup and Built-In Modes 
 Neither Garmin nor Apple sells a watch with a dedicated HYROX mode. The real difference in the Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX comparison is how much work stands between you and a clean set of splits. On setup, Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX comes down to a lap button versus an app.
 Garmin: Multisport Does the Job 
 According to the5krunner’s October 2026 testing , no Garmin watch has a built-in HYROX activity, so you build your own. Garmin’s own HYROX guide describes a multisport Brick profile that pairs Run (or Indoor Track) with Cardio, with transitions off and repeat on. Each press of the lap button then flips between run and station.
 This works on watches with multisport, which Garmin’s guide lists as the Fenix, Enduro, Instinct and Forerunner 255, 265, 955 and 965 families. Garmin’s Q1 2026 update also added a Mixed Session activity, but the same testing found it too clunky for a real race.
 Apps fill the gap. A paid Connect IQ app such as Hybrid Smash (listed at $8.49 in the US store) names every lap and lets you undo a wrong press, which a plain Cardio profile cannot do.
 Apple Watch: Great Hardware, Third-Party App Required 
 Apple’s Workout app offers Outdoor Run and Functional Strength Training, and you can mark segments by hand, but it has no run-and-station structure. Most athletes add an app such as ROXFIT, HyRhythm or Hyro to get HYROX templates and split tracking.
 That means one more app to install, update and trust on race morning. Apple’s watchOS 27 notes mention better indoor run distance tracking, not a HYROX mode.
 Coros: The Only Built-In Hybrid Mode of the Three 
 Coros added a Hybrid Fitness mode in its Spring 2026 update, with Race, Training and Test options. The Test option mirrors the HYROX P’F”T, a six-exercise fitness test that points you toward a division.
 In the5krunner’s trial on an older Apex 2 Pro , the mode logged time and heart rate for each leg but recorded zero reps. Treat it as a clean logger, not a rep counter, and check that your exact model supports Hybrid Fitness before you buy.
 Check 2: Lap Control and Indoor Distance 
 In the Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX matchup, lap control matters more than GPS. HYROX runs happen inside exhibition halls, so GPS pace is unreliable on every brand. In one Men Pro race tracked on a Forerunner 965 as an indoor run, the Hybrid Smash developer reports that the watch’s distance for the eight runs ranged from 932 m to 1,171 m. That is why you end every segment with a lap press, never with the distance.
 On lap control, Garmin has a dedicated lap button. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 has an Action Button that can mark segments, but the Series 12 has no Action Button and relies on touch and the crown. Coros watches combine a dial with physical buttons.
 ⚠️ 
 Warning 
 Turn off Auto Pause and Auto Lap before race day. A slow sled push can be mistaken for standing still and trimmed from your station time.
 Remember that you count your own laps. The 2026/27 rulebook says racers are responsible for counting their running laps, and venue lap screens are only a non-official aid. Missed laps carry real time penalties, which we break down in our guide to the most common HYROX penalties .
 Check 3: Heart Rate Accuracy Under Load 
 Heart rate is where the Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX gap shows most. Wrist sensors lose accuracy when you grip a sled rope or farmers carry handles. Independent HYROX data is thin, but Tom’s Guide ran a useful half-marathon comparison. In that test , the Forerunner 970 beat the previous-generation Apple Watch Ultra 3 on GPS and especially on heart rate accuracy. It was a running test, not a HYROX one, but it is the best independent comparison we found.
 Apple says the new Health Sensing System in the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is its most accurate heart rate sensor yet. We could not find independent race-style testing of it, so treat that as a claim until data appears.
 💡 
 Info 
 A Bluetooth chest strap fixes wrist-sensor drift on any brand. Coros sells its strap from $79, and Garmin and Polar make equivalents.
 Check 4: Battery Life and Durability 
 A HYROX race lasts one to two hours for most athletes, so in the Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX debate battery is a training question, not a race-day one. Apple lists the Ultra 4 at up to 50 hours of normal use, and up to 25 hours of outdoor workout tracking in Extended Workout mode. That is plenty for any race, but Apple Watches generally still need charging more often than Garmin or Coros models.
 Coros’s official spec lists the Pace 4 at up to 19 days of daily use with sleep tracking, or 6 days with the always-on display. Garmin’s Forerunner and Fenix lines are also built around multi-day battery, which suits a training week with six sessions.
 On build quality, sled handles and sandbags will test any watch, so a spare silicone strap is cheap insurance.
 Check 5: Data After the Race 
 All three brands can send workouts to Strava, and each has its own app for deeper analysis: Garmin Connect, Apple Health and Fitness, and the Coros app. For Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX analysis, what matters is the comparison. Your watch splits will not match the official result exactly, because the chip handles official timing.
 Use the watch for pacing and trends, then check the official numbers with our guide to checking your HYROX results . Our HYROX station times show what good splits look like by division, and where most athletes lose time shows which stations usually cost the most.
 Check 6: Price and Ecosystem 
 Price is the last check in the Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX decision. Prices below are US list prices we found in October 2026, and retailers often discount. The ecosystem matters as much as the sticker: Apple Watch only works with an iPhone, and the Series 12 and Ultra 4 need an iPhone 11 or later on iOS 27. Garmin and Coros watches work with both iPhone and Android.

 Common Mistakes When Choosing a HYROX Watch 
 Most athletes lose time on setup, not hardware. These are the mistakes that show up again and again in the Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX decision, whichever brand wins.
 Judging by GPS pace. Indoors, distance drifts, so your lap presses must define the splits.
 Leaving Auto Pause on. Slow stations can get trimmed from your recorded time.
 Testing the setup on race morning. Run a full or half simulation first.
 Paying for music or cellular. The 2026/27 singles rulebook forbids headphones and cell phones on the race floor.
 Skipping the rulebook. Check what you plan to wear before you arrive.
 💡 
 Info 
 The 2026/27 singles rulebook says any item not listed as permitted is prohibited by default. Smartwatches are not named in either list, so if you plan to race with anything beyond a standard sports watch, ask HYROX customer support before race day.
 Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX: The Final Verdict by Profile 
 Here is the direct answer to the Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX question, based on the kind of athlete you are. Independent running tests favor Garmin on GPS and heart rate, while Apple wins as an everyday smartwatch, and that split holds for HYROX too.
 Pick Garmin If You Want Control and Training Data 
 In the Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX verdict, Garmin wins on setup control: a dedicated lap button, multisport profiles on mid-range and flagship models, and structured workouts in Garmin Connect. Garmin’s guide lists the Forerunner 255, 265, 955 and 965 as compatible, so you do not need the $749.99 Forerunner 970 to get the same lap-button workflow.
 Pick Apple Watch If Your Life Runs on iPhone 
 For iPhone users, the Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX answer is the Ultra 4 ($799), the better all-round smartwatch, with a bigger battery than before and an Action Button for segments. Accept that you will rely on a third-party app for HYROX structure. On a tighter budget, the Series 12 starts at $399 but has no Action Button.
 Pick Coros If You Want the Cheapest Working Setup 
 The Pace 4 ($249) is the cheapest route outside Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX, and Coros’s Hybrid Fitness mode is the only built-in hybrid mode of the three brands. Confirm your model is supported, and expect no automatic rep counting based on early testing.
 ✅ 
 Success 
 Our Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX pick: a multisport Garmin for most athletes, the Ultra 4 only if you are iPhone-first, and the Coros Pace 4 when budget decides.
 Quick Action Plan: Set Up Your Watch Before Race Day 
 Whatever you buy, spend one evening on setup and one session on a test run. Here is the plan to finish your Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX choice, whichever side you pick.
 Choose your method: a Garmin multisport Brick profile, Coros Hybrid Fitness, or a HYROX app on Apple Watch.
 Turn off Auto Pause and Auto Lap, and switch GPS off for indoor runs.
 Set one clean screen: lap time, total time and heart rate.
 Practice lap presses with wet hands during a sled push and pull session .
 Pair a chest strap if you want clean heart rate data.
 Run a full or half simulation, and set a target with our HYROX finish time estimator .
 Charge the watch the night before and add it to your race day checklist .
 No bib yet? Turn on HYTRACK alerts first, so a sold-out event does not leave your new watch with nothing to time.
 For official formats and standards, refer to the official HYROX website .
 FAQ 
 Is Garmin better than Apple Watch for HYROX? 
 For most athletes, yes. In the Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX comparison, Garmin’s multisport profiles and lap button give you a working run-and-station setup without a third-party app, and an independent half-marathon test found the Forerunner 970 more accurate on heart rate than the Ultra 3.
 Does the Apple Watch have a HYROX mode? 
 No. In the Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX comparison, Apple Watch has no built-in HYROX mode, so athletes use third-party apps such as ROXFIT or HyRhythm. Amazfit, not Apple, is the official wearable and timekeeping partner of HYROX.
 Does Garmin have a HYROX activity profile? 
 Not built in, as of October 2026, which makes Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX closer than it looks. You create a multisport Brick profile (Run or Indoor Track plus Cardio), copy a Cardio activity, or use a Connect IQ app, and the setup takes one evening.
 Can I wear a smartwatch during a HYROX race? 
 Whichever side of Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX you pick, sports watches are a common sight on race floors, and official timing comes from your ankle chip. The singles rulebook bans headphones, cell phones, cameras and smart glasses but does not name smartwatches, so confirm with HYROX customer support if you are unsure.
 Is Coros good for HYROX? 
 Yes, as a budget option beside Garmin vs Apple Watch for HYROX. Coros added a Hybrid Fitness mode with Race, Training and Test options in 2026, and the Pace 4 costs $249. Early testing found it logs time and heart rate per leg but not reps, and supported models vary, so check yours.

 I’m so much in the habit of recording and tracking my workouts that when I started training for Hyrox, my first question was, "how will I track them?" I want to keep an eye on my heart rate, so that narrowed it down to watches rather than smart bands or rings . But which is best? I tried four different watches and found two clear winners—depending on what you want to focus on. 
 Hyrox is, of course, the hybrid fitness sport that blends running with strength-endurance activities. (I have an explainer on it here .) A typical Hyrox or hybrid fitness workout involves cardio and strength exercises, which you’ll usually switch between throughout. You’ll probably want to note when you switch exercises (by pressing a lap button on your tracker), and you may want to track rests. If running is involved, you might want to know your run distance. No matter what, you probably want to keep an eye on your heart rate.
 You don’t actually need a dedicated Hyrox mode to track a workout with your watch. Plenty of folks get by with their standard watch’s “gym cardio” or “indoor run” modes (though some of the stations won’t rack up any actual run mileage). But some watches do have a Hyrox or hybrid mode, so here’s what you’ll see if you use those.
 Best for runners: Coros Pace 4’s hybrid fitness mode

 The Coros is my favorite for casual training. I can walk into the gym, start a workout on the watch, and know that everything important is getting logged. During each segment of the workout, I can see a timer tracking the length of my exercise, as well as my heart rate on a color-coded graph.

 Coros automatically detects which segments were runs, and labels them as such when I view the workout on my phone later. The other segments are labeled as “functional training,” but I can edit the workout to properly label each one with the exercise I was doing. The best part is that Coros counts up your run mileage. As I’m leaving the gym, I’ll finish the workout on the watch, and get a little message that I racked up 2.73 miles in the process. I then use a voice note to jot down what the stations were, while they’re still fresh in my mind. 
 How to use it : Go into the activities menu and select Hybrid Fitness . I use Training mode with Manual rest , but if I know I’ll be jumping straight from activity to activity, I’ll select Continuous instead. Coros also has a mode for racing that shows your running pace during the run segments, and has the stations correctly labeled in order. There's also a mode for a fitness test similar to the Hyrox PFT .
 Best for following structured workouts: Roxfit with Apple Watch
 Credit: Beth Skwarecki
 I found Roxfit when I went looking for a way to track hybrid workouts with Garmin. While Roxfit does work on Garmin watches, I preferred using it with the Apple Watch. Roxfit is actually a standalone app; you don’t need a watch to use it. But if you create a workout in the Roxfit app, you can sync that workout to your watch, and your watch will guide you through the workout. Roxfit also has a ton of other Hyrox-focused features, letting you connect your past race times and upcoming events, and build a pacing plan for your next race. Today, I’m only concerned with guidance and tracking for ordinary workouts.

 There’s no way to track a freeform workout with Roxfit, but it’s easy to create a workout on the fly. Chat with “Hype” (the built-in chatbot) and ask it for whatever you need. You can also build a workout manually, but I found Hype tends to understand me pretty well. For example, I said, “Give me a workout with one minute of running and then 10 reps of lunges, repeated five times, no rest” and got exactly that.
 The Roxfit app will tell you when you’re halfway through each segment, count down your last three seconds of timed segments, and helpfully read your next steps out loud: “Now: run one minute. Next up: sandbag lunges.” The data fields on the Apple Watch are easy to read and understand, but the Garmin version is okay, too. If you use Garmin, note that the “send to wearable” button in the Roxfit app sends the workout to your Garmin app , not to the watch itself. You’ll still need to go to the Garmin Connect app to send it to the watch. 
 How to use it : On your phone, create a workout, and sync it to your Apple or Garmin watch. From your watch, select the workout and start it from there. There is no way to start a freeform workout where you choose what to do in real time.
 Runner-up: Amazfit’s Hyrox mode
 Hyrox mode on an Amazfit Active Max. Note that the fuzzy black bars are an artifact of taking the photo in sunny conditions; they aren't visible in real life.

 Of all the watches I’m discussing today, Amazfit is the only one that actually uses the word Hyrox. (Amazfit is an official partner of the Hyrox company.) Its Hyrox mode is similar to Coros’s, but doesn’t seem to count up running mileage or recognize running laps. Besides the “free” training mode, you can also use one of three timers: tabata (20 seconds work, 10 seconds rest, for four minutes), AMRAP (a set time cap for whatever you want to do), or EMOM (you’ll get an alert at the top of each minute to start your exercise, and then you rest for the remainder of the minute). 
 How to use it : From the activity menu, select Hyrox training . Use the lap button to create new laps or segments, or follow one of the timer modes. Runs will not be recognized, and run distance will not be tracked. There is also a race mode that labels each segment with its correct event (giving you a view with running pace for the running ones) and a mode for the Hyrox PFT test.
